heuristics: Pick the primary node by the paper's main methodological contribution, not the material it studies (a new MOF made by solvothermal synthesis is Synthesis > Reticular synthesis).

A paper that introduces a new instrument or measurement protocol belongs under the technique it advances; papers that only use routine characterization take their primary node from synthesis or computation.
Combined theory-experiment papers: choose Computation only when the calculations drive the discovery; otherwise the experimental method is primary and Computation is secondary.
Operando/in situ work goes under Electrochemical & device testing > Operando when the measurement is during operation; otherwise under the probe's own branch (e.g. In situ TEM).
ML papers whose output is a trained model or dataset go under Data-driven; ML used as a minor analysis tool is a secondary node at most.
Use the Application Tree (and the material-class facet) for what the material is for; keep the Method Tree for how the work was done.
